full_judgment:
5. The defendants contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. In their written statement, the defendants stated that the suit filed by the plaintiff is not maintainable in its present form and that it is barred by limitation. Their further case, in short, is that defendants' predecessor late Dalil Uddin Ahammed, a high official of British era, obtained permanent lease of the suit land from the then Sreephaltali Estate and had been paying rent. During SA record, said land measuring about 19.35 acres was properly and correctly recorded in the name of Dalil Uddin Ahammed. Later, in 1990 some interested people by making application to the Land Reform Board tried to declare the suit land as khas. On such application an enquiry was held and according to the enquiry a report submitted by the officers at the field and on the basis of ROR the evil design failed and property was properly recorded in the name of the defendants. The defendants have since been possessing the land by growing jackfruit trees, mango trees etc. and also fishing in the ponds and by paying rent up to 1994. The plaintiff never took any step for correction of record in any manner till the filing of the suit. 

 (II) The trial Court and the High Court Division have failed to consider that before acquisition of rent receiving interest there cannot be any cause of action to file an application under Section 19(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the rent receiving interest of Dhaka where the suit plot at the relevant time was situated having been acquired in the year 1963, the alleged case under Section 53 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is collusive and void and without considering the aforesaid legal provision the courts below relied upon the alleged judgment of Special Appeal No. 239 of 1962 in finding title in favour of the defendant respondent. 

 II. Whether the trial Court and the High Court Division have failed to consider that before acquisition of rent-receiving interest there cannot be any cause of action to file an application under Section 19(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the rent-receiving interest of Dhaka where the suit plot at the relevant time was situated having been acquired in the year 1963, the alleged case under Section 53 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is collusive and void and without considering the aforesaid legal provisions and whether the courts below erred in law in relying upon the judgment of Special Appeal No.239 of 1962 finding title in favour of the defendant-respondent.
